purpose: Extend the Go stable x-opencode-session header and a client User-Agent to the image-generation request path.
riskRationale: Fail-open, credential-blind header-only change; Zen path untouched; existing suite passes (46 tests, 151 assertions).

text: Correct, well-scoped parity fix: image payloads now derive a stable session via the same sha256-to-32-hex scheme and Go image requests carry a version-tracked UA, all fail-open with explicit headers preserved. Existing tests pass, but the new behavior ships without committed coverage.

reasoning: Logic, security, and repo hard-rules all check out, but new prompt-derivation and UA behavior has no committed test locking it in, so regression risk remains.

message: Prompt derivation is credential-blind (model + normalized prompt only, extras ignored) and reuses the identical hash scheme, preserving stable-session semantics.
Go-gate mirrors the text path exactly and every injection is fail-open; Zen requests pass through byte-identical.
UA tracks OpenCodeConnector\VERSION dynamically with a literal fallback and uses only defined()/constant() guards — no connectors_ai_* option reads, compliant with the wp.org credential-blind rule.

New derive_from_prompt / UA paths have no committed tests: SessionHeaderTest only covers chat payloads and ImageGenerationPathTest never asserts headers, so a future refactor could silently break the image session or UA while the suite stays green.
suggestion: Commit tests for: Go image prompt derives stable 32-hex matching derive_from_data; empty/missing prompt omits session but still sets UA; explicit User-Agent/session preserved case-insensitively; Zen image request stays header-free.

message: Go text path sends no User-Agent while Go image path now does, so the two Go surfaces are fingerprinted inconsistently; gateway observability or UA-gated logic may treat them differently.
suggestion: Either add the same UA injection to AbstractOpenCodeTextGenerationModel::createRequest or document why image-only UA is intentional.

message: Unused catch variable $e in both try/catch blocks (SessionHeader.php uses catch (\Throwable) without a variable); harmless but inconsistent.
suggestion: Drop the unused variable to match SessionHeader style.
